docs.title: What is the Codoc FHIR API?
docs.text: The Codoc FHIR API is a complete implementation of the FHIR R4B standard for managing hospital clinical data. It exposes the entire Codoc data model through standardized and interoperable FHIR resources.

docs.title: Available Resources
docs.text:
The API exposes 10 main FHIR resources:

Resource Description Use Case Patient Patient identity and demographics Patient records, IPP identifiers Organization Hospital structure (sites, departments, units) Organizational hierarchy Encounter Hospital stays and intra-hospital movements Patient pathway, admissions DocumentReference Clinical documents Reports, medical notes Observation Laboratory results and patient data Lab analyses Procedure Medical procedures Interventions, examinations MedicationRequest Medication prescriptions Prescriptions, treatments DiagnosticReport Diagnostic reports Imaging, EFR, ECG CodeSystem Medical vocabularies (thesaurus) ICD-10, ATC, local codes Phenotype NLP semantic enrichment Medical concept extraction

docs.title: Multi-Identifiers
docs.text:
All resources support multiple identifiers with different purposes:

  • use: "official" - Primary key in database (use this for API read operations)
  • use: "usual" - Identifier used in the hospital system (human-readable, context-specific)

Example with Patient resource: 

{
  "resourceType": "Patient",
  "id": "123",
  "identifier": [
    {"use": "official", "value": "123"},
    {"use": "usual", "system": "HIS", "value": "IPP123456"}
  ],
  "name": [{"family": "Smith", "given": ["John"]}]
}

In this example: - Use id: "123" or identifier.official: "123" for API read operations (GET) - identifier.usual: "IPP123456" is the patient's IPP number visible in the hospital

docs.title: Simplified Integration with Codoc Data Model
docs.text:
The FHIR API is built on top of Codoc's data model, providing seamless integration with all Codoc applications. Resources map directly to the hospital's internal entities:

  • Patient → Patient records in Codoc apps
  • Organization → Hospital structure (sites, departments, units)
  • Encounter → Patient stays and movements
  • Observation → Lab results, clinical measurements, and patient data
  • DocumentReference → Clinical documents and reports

This direct mapping eliminates transformation layers and ensures data consistency across all Codoc applications.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
API rate limiting

To protect API stability, rate limiting is enforced:

  • Anonymous users: 100 requests/hour
  • Authenticated users: 1,000 requests/hour

When the limit is reached, the API returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). Rate limits reset hourly.

docs.title: Read Operations
docs.text:
All resources support standard read operations:

Operation Method Endpoint Description Read GET /v4.3.0/{resource}/{id}/ Retrieve a resource by ID List (Search) GET /v4.3.0/{resource}/ Search resources with pagination

docs.title: List / Search
docs.text:
The List action retrieves a collection of resources with pagination support.

Endpoint: GET /v4.3.0/{resource}/

docs.title: Pagination Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Max Description _count 20 100 Number of resources per page page 1 - Page number for navigation

docs.title: Response Structure
docs.text:
The response is a FHIR Bundle of type searchset:

{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "searchset",
  "total": 45,
  "link": [
    {"relation": "self", "url": "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=10"},
    {"relation": "next", "url": "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=10&page=2"}
  ],
  "entry": [
    {"resource": {"resourceType": "Patient", "id": "1", ...}},
    {"resource": {"resourceType": "Patient", "id": "2", ...}}
  ]
}

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# List patients with 5 per page
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=5"

# Get page 2
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=5&page=2"

docs.title: FHIR Date Prefixes
docs.text:
Date filters (date, birthdate, death-date, _lastUpdated) support FHIR comparison prefixes:

Prefix Operator Example ge ≥ (greater than or equal) ?date=ge2024-01-01 le ≤ (less than or equal) ?date=le2024-12-31 gt > (strictly greater than) ?date=gt2024-01-01 lt < (strictly less than) ?date=lt2024-12-31 ne ≠ (not equal) ?date=ne2024-06-15

Prefixes can be combined: ?date=ge2024-01-01&date=le2024-12-31 retrieves all records from 2024.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}

API keys start with fhir_. Pass this header with every request.

docs.title: Key Permissions
docs.text:
Each API key is created with permissions scoped to specific FHIR resources. A key may grant access to one resource (e.g., Patient only), a subset, or all resources (*).

Contact your administrator to obtain a key or to adjust which resources it can access.

Public endpoints

CodeSystem, Concept, and Phenotype endpoints do not require authentication.

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Example 200 OK - Request successful Successful GET 401 Unauthorized - Authentication required Missing or invalid credentials 403 Forbidden - Insufficient permissions Valid credentials but no read access 404 Not Found - Resource not found Non-existent ID 429 Too Many Requests - Rate limit reached Over 1000 req/hour 500 Internal Server Error Application bug

docs.title: Automatic Logging
docs.text:
All FHIR requests are automatically logged via the FHIRAccessLogMiddleware middleware:

Recorded data: - User (ID or "anonymous") - IP address - HTTP method - Full URL - Headers (Content-Type, Accept, User-Agent) - HTTP status - Timestamps (start, end) - Processing duration

Confidentiality

Request bodies are never logged to protect health data.

docs.title: Bundle - Bulk Create
docs.text: Create multiple resources in a single HTTP request for optimal performance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Bundle endpoint allows you to create many resources at once (bulk create) instead of sending individual requests.

Endpoint: POST /v4.3.0/bundle/

docs.title: Why Use Bulk Create?
docs.text: Approach HTTP Requests SQL Queries Time Throughput Individual (100 resources) 100 407+ 6.7s 15/sec Bulk (type: transaction) 1 8 0.66s 150+/sec Gain -99% -98% -90% 10×

docs.title: 3 Simple Rules for Automatic Bulk
docs.text: When these 3 conditions are met, bulk optimization is automatically enabled:

docs.title: ✅ Rule 1: Use "type": "transaction"
docs.text:
{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "transaction",
  "entry": [...]
}

docs.title: ✅ Rule 2: At least 5 resources
docs.text:
{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "transaction",
  "entry": [
    {...},  // Resource 1
    {...},  // Resource 2
    {...},  // Resource 3
    {...},  // Resource 4
    {...}   // Resource 5 ← Minimum threshold
  ]
}

docs.title: ✅ Rule 3: Use "method": "POST" (create)
docs.text:
{
  "entry": [
    {
      "request": {
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "procedure"
      },
      "resource": {...}
    }
  ]
}

That's it! ✅ No extra parameters required (no ?enable_bulk=true, no special headers).

docs.title: Bundle Structure
docs.text:
{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "transaction",
  "entry": [
    {
      "request": {
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "procedure"
      },
      "resource": {
        "resourceType": "Procedure",
        "status": "completed",
        "code": {"coding": [{"code": "PROC001"}]},
        "subject": {"reference": "Patient/1"},
        "encounter": {"reference": "Encounter/10"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
Field Description resourceType Always "Bundle" type "transaction" (atomic) or "batch" (independent) entry[].request.method "POST" for create operations entry[].request.url Resource type in lowercase (e.g., procedure, observation) entry[].resource The FHIR resource to create

docs.title: Transaction Mode ("type": "transaction")
docs.text:
Behavior: All or Nothing

  • ✅ All resources created successfully → Success
  • ❌ One resource fails → Rollback all (nothing created)
  • 📊 Ideal for: Critical operations, linked data
{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "transaction",
  "entry": [...]
}

docs.title: Batch Mode ("type": "batch")
docs.text:
Behavior: Independent

  • ✅ Each resource created independently
  • ✅ Continues even if one fails (no rollback)
  • 📊 Ideal for: Large imports, non-critical data
{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "batch",
  "entry": [...]
}

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text:
Aspect Transaction Batch Atomicity ✅ Yes (all or nothing) ❌ No (independent) Bulk optimization ✅ Yes (optimal) ❌ No (slower) Rollback ✅ Automatic ❌ Manual Partial failure ❌ Fails all ✅ Creates the rest Performance ✅ Fast ⚠️ Slower Use case Critical operations Mass imports

Recommendation

Use "type": "transaction" for automatic bulk optimization!

docs.text:

docs.title: Pre-flight Checklist
docs.text:
• Valid JSON structure (no syntax errors)
  • type: "transaction" for bulk optimization
  • At least 5 resources (otherwise individual mode)
  • All resources have method: "POST"
  • All references exist (Patient, Encounter, codes)
  • Client timeout configured (recommended: 60s for 1000 resources)

docs.title: CodeSystem - Medical Vocabularies
docs.text: The CodeSystem resource represents medical thesauruses (ICD10, ATC, CCAM, custom vocabularies).

docs.title: Thesaurus
docs.text: GET /v4.3.0/codesystem/ GET /v4.3.0/codesystem/{code}/

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: GET /v4.3.0/codesystem/{code}/concept/ GET /v4.3.0/codesystem/{code}/concept/{concept_code}/

docs.title: Search Parameters
docs.text:
No filter parameters are available for CodeSystem. The full list of thesauruses is returned (paginated).

Public endpoint

This endpoint does not require authentication.

docs.title: CodeSystem (Thesaurus)
docs.text: FHIR Field Type Required Description url uri ✅ Yes Auto-generated: urn:codoc:fhir:codesystem:{code} identifier[] Identifier[] ✅ Yes 2 identifiers: official (ID) + usual (code) name string ✅ Yes Technical name (maps to Thesaurus.code) title string ✅ Yes (NOT Optional!) Full title (maps to Thesaurus.label) status code ✅ Yes ⚠️ Hardcoded "active" (not customizable) content code ✅ Yes ⚠️ Hardcoded "complete" (not customizable)

docs.title: Concept
docs.text: Field Type Required Description code code ✅ Yes Unique code in thesaurus display string ✅ Yes Concept label

docs.title: List Thesauruses
docs.text:
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/codesystem/?_count=20"

import requests

response = requests.get(
    "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/codesystem/",
    params={"_count": 20}
)

bundle = response.json()
print(f"Total: {bundle['total']} thesauruses")
for entry in bundle.get("entry", []):
    cs = entry["resource"]
    print(f"  {cs['name']}: {cs.get('title', 'N/A')}")

docs.title: Filter Observations by Thesaurus
docs.text:
You can list observations and filter by thesaurus on the application side:

import requests

# List observations with pagination
response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/observation/?_count=50")
bundle = response.json()

# Filter observations by COVID thesaurus
covid_observations = []
for entry in bundle.get('entry', []):
    obs = entry['resource']

    # Check if the code belongs to the COVID thesaurus
    system = obs['code']['coding'][0].get('system', '')
    if 'COVID_SYMPTOMES' in system:
        covid_observations.append(obs)

print(f"✅ {len(covid_observations)} COVID observations found")

docs.title: Retrieve and Decode a Document
docs.text:
Pythoncurl 
import base64
import requests

headers = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}
# Retrieve the document
response = requests.get("{API_URL}/v4.3.0/documentreference/456/", headers=headers)
doc = response.json()

# Decode the content
encoded_content = doc["content"][0]["attachment"]["data"]
html_content = base64.b64decode(encoded_content).decode()

print(f"Title: {doc['content'][0]['attachment'].get('title', 'N/A')}")
print(f"Date: {doc['date']}")
print(f"Content type: {doc['content'][0]['attachment']['contentType']}")
print(html_content)  # <p>Consultation report</p>

Navigate the Hierarchy
docs.text:
To navigate up the hierarchy, follow the partOf reference:

Python 
headers = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}

def get_parent_chain(org_id):
    """Retrieve complete parent chain."""
    chain = []
    current_id = org_id

    while current_id:
        org = requests.get(f"{API_URL}/v4.3.0/organization/{current_id}/", headers=headers).json()
        chain.append({
            "id": org["id"],
            "name": org["name"],
            "type": org["type"][0]["coding"][0]["code"]
        })

        if "partOf" in org:
            current_id = org["partOf"]["reference"].split("/")[-1]
        else:
            break

    return chain

# Example: find parents of a unit
chain = get_parent_chain("unit-5")
for i, org in enumerate(chain):
    print("  " * i + f"→ {org['name']} ({org['type']})")

docs.title: Getting Started with the Codoc FHIR API
docs.text: This section guides you through your first API calls with the Codoc FHIR API.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Codoc FHIR API is a RESTful API that implements the FHIR R4B standard. It requires:

  • ✅ An accessible Codoc FHIR server (HTTP/HTTPS)
  • ✅ An HTTP client (curl, Postman, or HTTP library)

docs.title: Quick Access
docs.text:
🚀 Quick Start

Your first API call in 5 minutes

Get Started →

docs.title: FHIR Resources
docs.text:
A resource is a business entity (Patient, Organization, Encounter, etc.). Each resource has:

  • A resourceType (e.g., "Patient")
  • A unique id
  • Required and optional fields
  • Relationships to other resources

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
The API exposes RESTful read endpoints for each resource:

GET    /v4.3.0/patient/        # List
GET    /v4.3.0/patient/123/    # Read

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The API supports versioning in the URL:

  • /v4.3.0/ - FHIR R4B (version 4.3.0) ✅ Recommended
  • /v5.0.0/ - FHIR R5 (version 5.0.0) ⚠️ Development (not available yet)

docs.title: Data Format
docs.text:
All exchanges use JSON:

Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
Advanced search coming soon

Basic LIST with pagination is supported (GET /v4.3.0/patient/), but FHIR search parameters (?name=Smith) are not yet implemented.

docs.title: 1. Verify the Connection
docs.text:
Start by verifying that the API responds:

curlPythonJavaScript 
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" {API_URL}/v4.3.0/metadata/

import requests

headers = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}
response = requests.get("{API_URL}/v4.3.0/metadata/", headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)  # Should display 200
print(response.json()["resourceType"])  # "CapabilityStatement"

fetch("{API_URL}/v4.3.0/metadata/")
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(data => {
    console.log(data.resourceType);  // "CapabilityStatement"
    console.log(data.fhirVersion);   // "4.3.0"
  });

Expected response: HTTP 200 with a FHIR CapabilityStatement object.

docs.text:

curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=10"

import requests

headers = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}
response = requests.get(
    "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/",
    params={"_count": 10},
    headers=headers
)

bundle = response.json()
print(f"Total: {bundle['total']} patients")
print(f"Page: {len(bundle.get('entry', []))} results")

for entry in bundle.get("entry", []):
    patient = entry["resource"]
    print(f"  - ID {patient['id']}: {patient.get('name', [{}])[0].get('family', 'N/A')}")

fetch("{API_URL}/v4.3.0/patient/?_count=10")
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(bundle => {
    console.log(`Total: ${bundle.total} patients`);
    bundle.entry?.forEach(entry => {
      const p = entry.resource;
      console.log(`  - ID ${p.id}: ${p.name?.[0]?.family ?? 'N/A'}`);
    });
  });

docs.title: What is a Thesaurus?
docs.text:
A thesaurus (or CodeSystem in FHIR) is a controlled vocabulary that contains medical concepts.

Examples of thesauri: - Biology: codes for lab tests (Hemoglobin, Blood Glucose, etc.) - Procedure: CCAM codes for medical procedures - Diagnosis: ICD-10 codes for diagnoses - Phenotypes: NLP concepts extracted from texts

docs.title: Step 3: Navigate the Parent Chain
docs.text:
To navigate up the hierarchy, follow the partOf reference:

Python 
def get_parent_chain(org_id):
    """Retrieve complete parent chain for an organization."""
    chain = []
    current_id = org_id

    while current_id:
        org = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/organization/{current_id}/", headers=HEADERS).json()
        chain.append({
            "id": org["id"],
            "name": org["name"],
            "type": org["type"][0]["coding"][0]["code"]
        })

        # Check if there is a parent
        if "partOf" in org:
            current_id = org["partOf"]["reference"].split("/")[-1]
        else:
            break

    return chain

# Example: find parents of a unit
unit_id = "unit-5"
chain = get_parent_chain(unit_id)

print(f"\n🔗 Hierarchical chain for unit ID {unit_id}:")
for i, org in enumerate(chain):
    indent = "  " * i
    print(f"{indent}→ {org['name']} ({org['type']})")

docs.title: Trace Patient Journey
docs.text: This guide explains how to retrieve a patient's complete journey from admission to discharge.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A patient journey consists of:

  1. Stay: global hospitalization record
  2. Movements: transfers between departments
  3. Documents: reports at each stage
  4. Observations: clinical and laboratory data

docs.title: Step 1: Retrieve the Stay
docs.text:
curlPython

curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" {API_URL}/v4.3.0/encounter/stay/789/

import requests

BASE_URL = "{API_URL}"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}
stay_id = 789

stay = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/encounter/stay/{stay_id}/", headers=HEADERS).json()

print(f"Stay ID: {stay['id']}")
print(f"Status: {stay['status']}")
print(f"Admission: {stay['period']['start']}")
if 'end' in stay.get('period', {}):
    print(f"Discharge: {stay['period']['end']}")
if 'serviceProvider' in stay:
    print(f"Service: {stay['serviceProvider']['reference']}")

docs.title: Step 2: Retrieve Movements
docs.text:
Movements are encounters with a partOf reference pointing to the stay:

Python 
# List all encounters and filter movements for this stay
encounters = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/encounter/",
    params={"_count": 100},
    headers=HEADERS
).json()

# Filter movements linked to this stay
movements = []
for entry in encounters.get("entry", []):
    enc = entry["resource"]
    if "partOf" in enc:
        parent_ref = enc["partOf"]["reference"]
        if str(stay_id) in parent_ref:
            movements.append(enc)

print(f"\n📍 MOVEMENTS ({len(movements)} total):")
for mvt in movements:
    period = mvt.get("period", {})
    start = period.get("start", "N/A")
    end = period.get("end", "in progress")
    service = mvt.get("serviceProvider", {}).get("display", "N/A")
    print(f"  [{mvt['status']}] {service}: {start} → {end}")

docs.title: Semantic Enrichment with Phenotypes
docs.text: This guide explains how to query phenotypes extracted from clinical documents.

docs.title: Concept
docs.text:
Phenotypes are medical concepts (symptoms, diagnoses, treatments) automatically extracted from document text using NLP (natural language processing).

Example:

"The patient has arterial hypertension and chest pain."

→ 2 phenotypes extracted: HYPERTENSION, CHEST_PAIN

docs.title: Step 1: List Phenotype Observations
docs.text:
Pythoncurl 
import requests

BASE_URL = "{API_URL}"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Api-Key {API_KEY}"}

# List all phenotypes with pagination
response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/observation/phenotype/?_count=50", headers=HEADERS)
bundle = response.json()

print(f"Total phenotypes: {bundle['total']}")
for entry in bundle.get('entry', []):
    pheno = entry['resource']
    print(f"\n📋 Phenotype ID: {pheno['id']}")
    print(f"   Code: {pheno['code']['coding'][0]['code']}")
    print(f"   Display: {pheno['code']['coding'][0]['display']}")
    print(f"   Value: {pheno['valueString']}")

    # Display components (semantic type, relevance score, etc.)
    for component in pheno.get('component', []):
        comp_code = component['code'].get('text', component['code'].get('coding', [{}])[0].get('code', ''))
        comp_value = component.get('valueString', component.get('valueDecimal', component.get('valueInteger')))
        print(f"   {comp_code}: {comp_value}")

curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key {API_KEY}" "{API_URL}/v4.3.0/observation/phenotype/?_count=50"

docs.title: Step 2: Retrieve a Specific Phenotype
docs.text:
Python 
phenotype_id = 42
pheno = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/observation/phenotype/{phenotype_id}/", headers=HEADERS).json()

print(f"Concept: {pheno['code']['coding'][0]['display']}")
print(f"Text found: {pheno['valueString']}")
print(f"Date: {pheno['effectiveDateTime']}")
print(f"Patient: {pheno['subject']['reference']}")
print(f"Source document: {pheno['derivedFrom'][0]['reference']}")

docs.title: Step 3: Retrieve the Source Document
docs.text:
Each phenotype is linked to a DocumentReference via derivedFrom:

Python 
import base64

# From the phenotype, get the source document
doc_ref = pheno["derivedFrom"][0]["reference"]
doc_id = doc_ref.split("/")[-1]

doc = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/v4.3.0/documentreference/{doc_id}/", headers=HEADERS).json()

# Decode the document content
encoded = doc["content"][0]["attachment"]["data"]
content = base64.b64decode(encoded).decode()

print(f"\nSource document: {doc['content'][0]['attachment'].get('title', 'N/A')}")
print(f"Date: {doc['date']}")
print(f"Content preview: {content[:500]}...")

docs.title: What is an Implementation Guide?
docs.text:
A FHIR Implementation Guide (IG) is a set of rules about how FHIR resources are used to solve a particular problem. It includes:

  • Profiles - Constraints on FHIR resources for specific use cases
  • Extensions - Custom data elements not in the base specification
  • Value Sets - Allowed code values for coded elements
  • Code Systems - Custom terminologies
  • Capability Statement - Server behavior definition

docs.title: Phenotype Observation Components
docs.text:
Component Pattern

Phenotype metadata is implemented using the Observation.component pattern following FHIR best practices. This provides better tool support and clearer semantic meaning than extensions.

The CodocPhenotypeObservation profile uses sliced components with codes from the CodocPhenotypeComponentsCS code system:

Component Slice Code Value Type Description phenotypeFlag phenotype Integer Phenotype flag (0 or 1) semanticType semantic_type String UMLS semantic type (Disease, Symptom, Finding, etc.) tfidfScore tfidf_code_document Quantity TF-IDF relevance score (0.0 - 1.0) countConcept count_concept Integer Concept occurrence count in document countStrFound count_concept_str_found Integer String fragment occurrence count

  "resourceType": "Observation",
  "status": "final",
  "code": {

  },
  "subject": {"reference": "Patient/1"},
  "derivedFrom": [{"reference": "DocumentReference/10"}],
  "valueString": "essential hypertension",
  "component": [
    {
      "code": {"coding": [{"code": "phenotype"}]},
      "valueInteger": 1
    },
    {
      "code": {"coding": [{"code": "semantic_type"}]},
      "valueString": "Disease"
    },
    {
      "code": {"coding": [{"code": "tfidf_code_document"}]},
      "valueQuantity": {"value": 0.85}
    },
    {
      "code": {"coding": [{"code": "count_concept"}]},
      "valueInteger": 2
    },
    {
      "code": {"coding": [{"code": "count_concept_str_found"}]},
      "valueInteger": 1
    }
  ]
}
